statement: The table below gives selected values of the function $f$. $$\begin{array}{c|cccccc} x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 \\ \hline f(x) & 7 & 4 & 9 & -2 & 6 & 1 \end{array}$$ The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = 3f(x - 2) + 1$. What is the value of $g(4)$?

choices.misconception: I put $4$ straight into $f$ and used $f(4) = -2$, so I got $3(-2) + 1 = -5$, forgetting the $-2$ inside the parentheses.
I thought $x - 2$ meant I should move two places to the right in the table, so I used $f(6) = 1$ and got $3 \cdot 1 + 1 = 4$.
I found $f(2) = 4$ but added the $1$ before multiplying by $3$, so I got $3(4 + 1) = 15$.

hints: Start on the inside: when $x = 4$, what number goes into $f$?
The input to $f$ is $x - 2 = 2$. Read $f(2)$ from the table, then multiply by $3$ and add $1$.
$g(4) = 3f(2) + 1$, and the table gives $f(2) = 4$, so compute $3 \cdot 4 + 1$.

solutions.reliable: Substitute $x = 4$ into the definition: $g(4) = 3f(4 - 2) + 1 = 3f(2) + 1$. The table gives $f(2) = 4$, so $g(4) = 3 \cdot 4 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13$.
